name: Prize crossword No 23,269
preamble: Because of the symmetry of the diagram, acrosses and downs would be interchangeable; please arrange it so that the six solutions featuring seven similarly placed men all go across.

clue.text: A game bird's roost at Christmas: hence comes William

definitions.text: A game bird's roost at Christmas

blocks.clueFragment: A game bird's roost at Christmas
blocks.note: first meaning: in the carol The Twelve Days of Christmas, the partridge sits in this
second meaning: the Williams is a variety of pear, so it grows on one of these

explanation.surface: A seasonal riddle about where a festive game bird perches, and what a man called William has to do with it.
explanation.walkthrough: The partridge of the Christmas carol roosts in this tree; William is not a man but the Williams pear, a common British variety of the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The carol's first gift is a partridge perched in such a tree, and a Williams is a well-known kind of pear grown on one.

clue.text: At last it matters not which second J

blocks.note: Z is the very last letter of the alphabet
'any' is what you say when it makes no difference which one

explanation.surface: A shrug of indifference about which of two letters comes second.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cross-reference: the two entries numbered 22 both begin with J, and the printed list gave downs first, so the second J is the across one, JESTER. A zany was a clown's assistant, so ZANY means a jester.
explanation.definitionFit: A zany was originally the comic servant who mimicked the clown, so the word names a buffoon or professional fool.

clue.text: Nike? - had son by arrow cleft

blocks.note: first meaning, playful: Nike is the Greek goddess of victory, so a god of winning, split as GOD and WIN
second meaning: the Earl of Wessex whose son Harold was killed by an arrow at Hastings in 1066

explanation.surface: A sporting brand's name followed by a grisly note about a son split by an arrow.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'Nike' is read as GOD + WIN, the deity of victory. Earl Godwin was the father of King Harold, traditionally shot in the eye at the Battle of Hastings.
explanation.definitionFit: Godwin, Earl of Wessex, fathered Harold II, the English king said to have died from an arrow wound in 1066.

clue.text: Arrange in lines: check round where song's begun

indicators.note: what has only just begun shows nothing but its opening letter
going round something means surrounding it on both sides

blocks.note: to check something is to verify it
the opening letter of song

explanation.surface: Instructions for laying out lyrics: check them over from the point where the song starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrange in lines' sounds like drilling soldiers, but the lines are lines of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: To versify is to put material into verse, which means setting it out in metrical lines.

clue.text: Prince keeping somewhat posh, as thing of course

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece is held within the other

blocks.note: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V
somewhat means a bit
U means upper-class, as in Nancy Mitford's U and non-U

explanation.surface: A royal who stays a little bit grand, as you would expect him to.
explanation.walkthrough: U is a British label for upper-class usage, from the 1950s 'U and non-U' debate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something habitual is done regularly by custom, the way things happen as a matter of course.

clue.text: Columns describing various brigs on Dee

indicators.note: various suggests many different versions, so the letters may come in any arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Newspaper columns written about assorted sailing ships on the River Dee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Columns' suggests journalism or architecture; here it means spinal columns. The Dee is a river in Scotland and another in Wales and England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridge bone is an old word for the backbone, and the vertebral or spinal column is the anatomical name for the same thing.

clue.text: Things told a student, soon to drop a horse

blocks.note: information, things you are told
taken as written
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student is warned they will soon be thrown off a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop' sounds like a rider falling or dropping a course, but it means to give birth, as animals do.
explanation.definitionFit: A mare that is pregnant is said to be carrying a foal, and will soon give birth to a young horse.

clue.text: In general, Nail - and one might add, Touch not

indicators.note: being in something means lying inside it, enclosed by it

blocks.note: Robert E. Lee, Confederate general
a talon is a claw, the nail of a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A general named Nail issues a do-not-touch order, with an afterthought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General, Nail' reads like a rank and surname; the general is Lee and the nail is a claw.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for 'not to mention', an addition to what was said, and also an order to leave something untouched.

clue.text: For Celia, tale within and tales without

indicators.note: something within is held inside another thing
in its old sense without means outside, so this piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or table talk about a person
a tale is a lie, as in telling tales

explanation.surface: A story told inside other stories, offered on behalf of a woman named Celia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside, so the tales go round the tale. 'For Celia' means standing in for her: it is her alias.
explanation.definitionFit: In As You Like It, Celia flees to Arden in disguise and takes the assumed name Aliena, so it stands for her.

clue.text: Cross fish has power to view what's not on view

definitions.text: power to view what's not on view

blocks.note: an X is a cross
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: An angry fish with the superpower of seeing hidden things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective meaning angry, describing the fish; it is the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiation of this kind passes through flesh and objects, letting doctors and security staff see hidden bones or contents.

clue.text: The seat of power existed: nothing's new

indicators.note: making something new means remaking it in a different form

blocks.note: existed means was
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cynic's view of government: the old seat of power existed, but there's nothing new.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is': nothing is new. The answer is also the first US president, one of the theme's men.
explanation.definitionFit: Washington DC is the US capital, home of the White House and Congress, so it is where American government sits.

clue.text: Harry, said Fred, has liquor in first B

indicators.note: something in another thing sits enclosed by it

blocks.note: the first B entry, printed before its across twin, is BEAT, and to beat is to tan
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Fred reports that Harry has been drinking in the first bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Truman's surname sounds like that of Fred Trueman, the Yorkshire and England fast bowler. 'First B' points to the B entries at 24: the downs were printed first, and to tan a hide is to beat it.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry S. Truman was the 33rd US president, and said aloud his surname matches the famous cricketer Fred's.

clue.text: Composer, one that follows change to men

indicators.note: to change something is to alter its form, so these letters take a new order
following means coming after, so this piece is placed second

blocks.note: taken as written
one composer, picking up the word before: Verdi

explanation.surface: A composer who follows a sex change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' means one composer, echoing the definition, and the solver must find a particular one, Verdi, to put last.
explanation.definitionFit: Claudio Monteverdi was an Italian composer of the early Baroque, best known for the opera L'Orfeo and his Vespers.

clue.text: A golfing match: the kidnapped boy turned left

indicators.note: turning something round brings its back part to the front

blocks.note: David Balfour is the young hero of Stevenson's novel Kidnapped
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A sports report in which a golfer, once a kidnap victim, turns to the left.
explanation.walkthrough: Lower case hides the title: it is Kidnapped, by Robert Louis Stevenson. The last four letters of the boy's surname move to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf this is a match format with two pairs of players, each person playing their own ball throughout.

clue.text: Know, heartless ass, this party-leading Scot?

indicators.note: with no heart, the central part is taken away

blocks.note: ken is a Scots verb meaning to know
a neddy is a donkey

explanation.surface: A question put to a foolish person: do you know this Scottish party leader?
explanation.walkthrough: Of the two middle Ds, one is dropped. Charles Kennedy, a Scot, led the Liberal Democrats; the surname also belongs to the theme's president.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Kennedy, MP for a Highland seat, was leader of the Liberal Democrats from 1999 until early 2006.

clue.text: Bird, easy thing and hard, cop must retain

indicators.note: retaining something means holding on to it inside

blocks.note: a dick is slang for a detective
as easy as ABC
H is the pencil marking for hard

explanation.surface: A policeman is told to hang on to a bird, something easy and something hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Easy thing' stands for ABC, from the phrase 'as easy as ABC'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dabchick is the everyday name for the little grebe, a small diving waterbird of ponds and rivers.

clue.text: Bill Heathcliff loved initially when wed

blocks.note: Heathcliff's beloved is Catherine, whose initial is C
Catherine marries Edgar Linton and takes his name

explanation.surface: Someone named Bill whom Heathcliff loved at first, back when he was married.
explanation.walkthrough: In Wuthering Heights Catherine Earnshaw loves Heathcliff but marries Edgar Linton, becoming Catherine Linton. 'Bill' looks like an invoice; it is a first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Clinton was the 42nd president of the United States, serving two terms in the 1990s.

clue.text: For "nought" write "cross": continuing source of ill I am

blocks.note: nought is zero, written as O
to pen is to write
cross and sore both mean annoyed

explanation.surface: An instruction in noughts and crosses: write a cross where a nought would go.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it look like swapping one symbol for another; each word is just a separate piece. The answer speaks for itself in 'I am'.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally an unhealed wound, the phrase is used figuratively for a grievance that keeps causing trouble and resentment.

clue.text: Fen stream splits rocks, whereon great ships we see

indicators.note: splitting something opens it up so another piece can sit inside

blocks.note: to rock is to sway
an ea is a river or drainage channel in the Fens of eastern England

explanation.surface: A small Fenland stream cuts through rocks, while big ships sail past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocks' looks like a noun, stones in the stream; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaways are shipping routes or channels deep enough for ocean-going vessels, such as the St Lawrence Seaway.

clue.text: First lady, centre of activity?

blocks.note: first meaning: a woman who dominates her circle
second meaning: the hive's fertile female, at the heart of all that busy work

explanation.surface: A president's wife described as the hub of everything going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady' suggests the president's wife, fitting the theme, but here it is the leading woman of a group; the question mark marks the hive joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a domineering woman at the top of a social set and the single egg-laying female round which a hive works.

clue.text: The public service workers sing as one

blocks.note: first meaning: the name of Britain's largest public-sector trade union
second meaning: singing the same notes together, as in 'sing in' this

explanation.surface: Public sector employees join together in a song.
explanation.walkthrough: UNISON is the British trade union for public service staff such as council and health workers.
explanation.definitionFit: The union takes its name from the word for voices sounding the same note together, which is also what acting in agreement means.

clue.text: Who's good in mockery? Fool that's not an ass

blocks.note: first meaning: someone skilled at teasing and making fun
second meaning: a court fool, a professional comic and no real idiot

explanation.surface: A question about who excels at ridicule, answered by a fool who is no idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool' and 'ass' look like synonyms; the point is that a court fool was clever, playing the fool for a living.
explanation.definitionFit: The court entertainer earned his keep by joking and teasing, and the wise fool of Shakespeare is often the sharpest mind present.

clue.text: No clear fresh words we need - just start to gas

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of just
argon is an inert gas

explanation.surface: A plea for plain new language, not hot air: just get started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' reads as idle talk, which fits the surface, but it is the chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Jargon is specialist terminology that outsiders find obscure, and it is often stale and formulaic rather than plain.

clue.text: General that is retired on points in rain

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the letters run backwards
being in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: i.e. is short for id est, that is
a shower is a spell of rain
E and N, east and north, are compass points

explanation.surface: A retired general stands his ground on points of principle out in the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' means placed after. Dwight D. Eisenhower was Supreme Allied Commander in Europe before becoming the 34th US president.
explanation.definitionFit: Eisenhower was a five-star US Army general who led the D-Day landings before entering politics.

clue.text: ... a plant or plants proclaiming wine, it's said

blocks.note: first meaning: a shrub, or an area of scrubland covered in them
second meaning: a branch of ivy once hung outside a tavern as its sign, hence the proverb 'good wine needs no' one

explanation.surface: The ellipsis continues 24-down's 'beat about the', then names a plant used to advertise wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'good wine needs no bush' recalls the old vintner's sign. The ellipsis completes the idiom with 24-down, and the answer is two presidents, father and son, making seven men.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub is a single plant and the bush is also wild scrubland, while a vintner's ivy sign advertised his wine.

clue.text: Are placed where cops are placed: some do about ...

blocks.note: be is the root form of the verb whose plural present is are
to be placed somewhere is to be located at it

explanation.surface: Officers stationed at their posts, while others go round evasively.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on to 24-across: some people beat about the bush, avoiding the point. A police officer's patrol route is his beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A beat is the area a constable patrols, and people who avoid the point are said to do this about the bush.

clue.text: Austen or Dickens compassed such as Sven

indicators.note: to compass something is to encircle it, so these names enclose the letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first name, the little word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Two great English novelists compared with a Swedish man.
explanation.walkthrough: Sven is a typical Scandinavian first name, as borne by the Swedish football manager Sven-Göran Eriksson.
explanation.definitionFit: Nordic describes the people of Scandinavia and its neighbours, and a man called Sven is likely to be one.

clue.text: Farmers as troops on line - perhaps one may

blocks.note: one farmer or troop member might be this smallholder
RY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Farmers lined up like soldiers, as some of them may well be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On line' places a railway after the single member: a yeoman, perhaps, may be on the line. The yeomanry were British volunteer cavalry drawn from farming men.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both small landowning farmers as a class and the volunteer mounted regiments they formed.
